findings.title: Priority inversion: bm_high waited on bm_low via a semaphore
findings.summary: bm_high (prio 30) was blocked 20.20 ms on a semaphore (0x00000027038bb068) released by bm_low (prio 10); for 20.19 ms of that, bm_low was ready but bm_med (prio 20), proc_pool_thread (prio 21) held its CPU. Seen 40x.
findings.qnx_note: QNX semaphores have no owner, so the kernel cannot apply priority inheritance. A pthread mutex (priority inheritance is the QNX default) would have boosted bm_low to priority 30 and the medium-priority work could not have preempted it.

findings.title: Unusual behaviour in bm_high
findings.summary: bm_high (prio 30) behaved unlike healthy QNX programs in 80 of its 80 time windows; the most unusual stretch lasted 80 ms. It stands out in: time blocked on a semaphore (higher than healthy), time blocked while a lower-priority thread held its CPU (higher than healthy), longest single block (higher than healthy). The closest pattern TraceLens has seen is priority inversion through a semaphore used as a lock, but only loosely (distance 7.84 against 1.062 typical for it): treat this as behaviour of its own.
findings.qnx_note: Learned from healthy QNX 8.0 traces: this thread behaved unlike any healthy run in the features listed. It is not a proven bug and gets no automatic fix: look at the timeline around it. Any resemblance to a known pattern is measured against labelled example windows, never a rule that fired.

findings.title: Unusual behaviour in bm_low
findings.summary: bm_low (prio 10) behaved unlike healthy QNX programs in 80 of its 80 time windows; the most unusual stretch lasted 80 ms. It stands out in: longest wait for a CPU (higher than healthy), time waiting for a CPU (higher than healthy), time asleep (lower than healthy). The closest pattern TraceLens has seen is healthy_irq_deferred (distance 0.23, inside the 0.852 typical for that pattern).
findings.qnx_note: Learned from healthy QNX 8.0 traces: this thread behaved unlike any healthy run in the features listed. It is not a proven bug and gets no automatic fix: look at the timeline around it. Any resemblance to a known pattern is measured against labelled example windows, never a rule that fired.
